source: (The cabin; by the stern windows; Ahab sitting alone, and gazing out.)
I leave a white and turbid wake; pale waters, paler cheeks, where’er I sail. The envious billows sidelong swell to whelm my track; let them; but first I pass.

Yonder, by ever-brimming goblet’s rim, the warm waves blush like wine. The gold brow plumbs the blue. The diver sun—slow dived from noon—goes down; my soul mounts up! she wearies with her endless hill. Is, then, the crown too heavy that I wear? this Iron Crown of Lombardy. Yet is it bright with many a gem; I the wearer, see not its far flashings; but darkly feel that I wear that, that dazzlingly confounds. ’Tis iron—that I know—not gold. ’Tis split, too—that I feel; the jagged edge galls me so, my brain seems to beat against the solid metal; aye, steel skull, mine; the sort that needs no helmet in the most brain-battering fight!

Dry heat upon my brow? Oh! time was, when as the sunrise nobly spurred me, so the sunset soothed. No more. This lovely light, it lights not me; all loveliness is anguish to me, since I can ne’er enjoy. Gifted with the high perception, I lack the low, enjoying power; damned, most subtly and most malignantly! damned in the midst of Paradise! Good night—good night! (waving his hand, he moves from the window.)

’Twas not so hard a task. I thought to find one stubborn, at the least; but my one cogged circle fits into all their various wheels, and they revolve. Or, if you will, like so many ant-hills of powder, they all stand before me; and I their match. Oh, hard! that to fire others, the match itself must needs be wasting! What I’ve dared, I’ve willed; and what I’ve willed, I’ll do! They think me mad—Starbuck does; but I’m demoniac, I am madness maddened! That wild madness that’s only calm to comprehend itself! The prophecy was that I should be dismembered; and—Aye! I lost this leg. I now prophesy that I will dismember my dismemberer. Now, then, be the prophet and the fulfiller one. That’s more than ye, ye great gods, ever were. I laugh and hoot at ye, ye cricket-players, ye pugilists, ye deaf Burkes and blinded Bendigoes! I will not say as schoolboys do to bullies—Take some one of your own size; don’t pommel me! No, ye’ve knocked me down, and I am up again; but ye have run and hidden. Come forth from behind your cotton bags! I have no long gun to reach ye. Come, Ahab’s compliments to ye; come and see if ye can swerve me. Swerve me? ye cannot swerve me, else ye swerve yourselves! man has ye there. Swerve me? The path to my fixed purpose is laid with iron rails, whereon my soul is grooved to run. Over unsounded gorges, through the rifled hearts of mountains, under torrents’ beds, unerringly I rush! Naught’s an obstacle, naught’s an angle to the iron way!

modern_en.title: Chapter 37 — Sunset
paragraphs: The cabin, by the stern windows. Ahab sitting alone, gazing out.
I leave a white and troubled wake. Pale waters, paler cheeks, wherever I sail. The jealous waves swell sideways to swallow my track. Let them — but first I pass.

Out there, at the ever-brimming goblet's rim, the warm waves blush like wine. The golden brow plumbs the blue. The diver sun — slowly dived from noon — goes down. My soul mounts up! She tires of her endless hill. Is, then, the crown too heavy that I wear? This Iron Crown of Lombardy. Yet it is bright with many a gem. I, the wearer, cannot see its distant flashing — but I darkly feel that I wear something that dazzlingly confounds. It is iron — that I know — not gold. It is cracked, too — I feel it. The jagged edge chafes me so, my brain seems to beat against the solid metal. Yes, a steel skull, mine — the kind that needs no helmet in the most brain-battering fight!

Dry heat upon my brow? Oh! There was a time when the sunrise nobly stirred me and the sunset soothed. No more. This lovely light — it doesn't light me. All beauty is agony to me, since I can never enjoy it. Gifted with the high perception, I lack the low, enjoying power. Damned — most subtly and most cruelly! Damned in the midst of Paradise! Good night — good night! (Waving his hand, he moves from the window.)

It was not so hard a task. I expected to find at least one man stubborn, but my one geared circle fits into all their various wheels, and they revolve. Or, if you prefer, like so many anthills of gunpowder, they all stand before me — and I am their match. Oh, how hard! That to set others ablaze, the match itself must burn away! What I have dared, I have willed. And what I have willed, I will do! They think me mad — Starbuck does. But I am demonic. I am madness maddened! That wild madness that is calm only to comprehend itself! The prophecy said I would be dismembered — and yes! I lost this leg. I now prophesy that I will dismember my dismemberer. So let the prophet and the fulfiller be one. That's more than you great gods ever were. I laugh at you and hoot at you, you cricket-players, you boxers, you deaf Burkes and blinded Bendigoes! I will not say as schoolboys say to bullies: pick on someone your own size, don't pummel me! No — you've knocked me down, and I am up again. But you have run and hidden. Come out from behind your cotton bags! I have no long gun to reach you. Come, Ahab sends his compliments — come and see if you can swerve me. Swerve me? You cannot swerve me — or else you swerve yourselves! There, man has you. Swerve me? The path to my fixed purpose is laid with iron rails, and my soul is grooved to run on them. Over unsounded gorges, through the rifled hearts of mountains, under the beds of torrents, I rush unerringly! Nothing is an obstacle, nothing is an angle on the iron way!

modern_da.title: Kapitel 37 — Solnedgang
paragraphs: Kahytten, ved agtervinduerne. Ahab sidder alene og ser ud.
Jeg efterlader et hvidt og uroligt kølvand. Blege vande, blegere kinder, hvor end jeg sejler. De jaloux bølger svulmer ind fra siden for at sluge mit spor. Lad dem — men først sejler jeg forbi.

Derude, ved randen af det evigt fyldte bæger, rødmer de varme bølger som vin. Den gyldne pande sonderer det blå. Dykkersolen — der langsomt dykkede fra middag — går ned. Min sjæl stiger! Hun er træt af sin endeløse bakke. Er da kronen for tung, den jeg bærer? Denne jernkrone fra Lombardiet. Og dog er den lysende af mange ædelsten. Jeg, som bærer den, kan ikke se dens fjerne glimt — men jeg føler dunkelt, at jeg bærer noget, der blænder og forvirrer. Den er af jern — det ved jeg — ikke af guld. Den er revnet også — det føler jeg. Den takkede kant gnaver mig så, at min hjerne synes at slå mod det faste metal. Ja, en stålskalle, min — en, der ikke behøver nogen hjelm i den mest hjernebankende kamp!

Tør hede over min pande? Åh! Der var en tid, da solopgangen rørte mig ædelt, og solnedgangen beroligede. Ikke mere. Dette dejlige lys — det lyser ikke for mig. Al skønhed er pine for mig, siden jeg aldrig kan nyde den. Begavet med den høje opfattelse mangler jeg den lave evne til at nyde. Forbandet — mest snedigt og mest grusomt! Forbandet midt i Paradis! Godnat — godnat! (Han vinker med hånden og går væk fra vinduet.)

Det var ikke så svær en opgave. Jeg havde ventet at finde mindst én stædig mand, men mit ene tandhjul passer ind i alle deres forskellige hjul, og de drejer rundt. Eller hvis man foretrækker det: Som så mange myretuer af krudt står de alle foran mig — og jeg er deres tændstik. Åh, hvor hårdt! At for at sætte andre i brand må tændstikken selv brænde op! Det, jeg har vovet, har jeg villet. Og det, jeg har villet, vil jeg gøre! De tror, jeg er gal — Starbuck gør. Men jeg er dæmonisk. Jeg er vanvid, der er blevet gjort vanvittigt! Det vilde vanvid, der kun er roligt for at fatte sig selv! Profetien sagde, at jeg ville blive lemlæstet — og ja! Jeg mistede dette ben. Nu spår jeg, at jeg vil lemlæste ham, der lemlæstede mig. Så lad profeten og opfylderen være én. Det er mere, end I store guder nogensinde var. Jeg ler af jer og hyler ad jer, I kricketspillere, I boksere, I døve Burker og blinde Bendigoer! Jeg vil ikke sige, som skoledrenge siger til bøller: Tag en på din egen størrelse, slå mig ikke! Nej — I har slået mig ned, og jeg er oppe igen. Men I er løbet og har gemt jer. Kom frem bag jeres bomuldsballer! Jeg har ingen langskydende bøsse til at nå jer. Kom, Ahab sender sine komplimenter — kom og se, om I kan få mig til at give efter. Få mig til at give efter? I kan ikke få mig til at give efter — ellers giver I selv efter! Dér har mennesket jer. Få mig til at give efter? Vejen til mit faste mål er lagt med jernskinner, og min sjæl er rillet til at løbe på dem. Over ubundne kløfter, gennem bjergenes opskårne hjerter, under strømmenes senge suser jeg uden at fejle! Intet er en hindring, intet er en vinkel på jernvejen!
